title: Boeuf Bourguignon
subtitle: French slow-braised beef in red wine with bacon and mushrooms
excerpt: Boeuf bourguignon is one of the great French braises: chunks of beef braised for three hours in red wine with smoked bacon, pearl onions, and mushrooms until the meat is fall-apart tender and the wine has reduced to a thick, glossy, intensely savoury sauce. It is one of the defining dishes of French home cooking and one of the most satisfying things you can make in a pot.
sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon originates in Burgundy, where the combination of red wine and beef is foundational. The dish was codified in French cuisine by Auguste Escoffier in the early 20th century and brought to international attention by Julia Child in 1961. Beef chuck or shin gives the best result -- both have enough collagen to produce a rich, silky braise.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a large pot. Better over 2 to 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made a day ahead. Refrigerate overnight -- the fat rises and can be lifted off, and the flavour deepens.

content.text: The key to bourguignon is browning the beef well. Work in batches and do not crowd the pan -- a steamed grey piece of beef will not give the rich colour the dish needs. Use beef chuck: it has the right fat marbling and collagen to become tender in the wine. Shin also works. Do not use lean cuts -- they dry out.

Preheat the oven to 150C. Pat {{beef-chuck}} beef dry and season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a large ovenproof pot over high heat. Brown the beef in batches until deep brown on all sides, about 8 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Fry {{smoked-bacon}} bacon until crisp, about 4 minutes. Add {{shallots}} shallots and {{carrots}} carrots. Cook for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic, {{tomato-puree}} tomato puree, and {{plain-flour}} flour. Stir for 1 minute.

Pour in {{red-wine}} wine and {{beef-stock}} stock. Add {{thyme-fresh}} thyme and {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves. Return the beef. Bring to a simmer. Cover and place in the oven for 2.5 to 3 hours until the beef is completely tender.

In the last 20 minutes, saute {{mushrooms-chestnut}} mushrooms in {{unsalted-butter}} butter over high heat until browned. Add to the pot. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Serve with mash, egg noodles, or crusty bread.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 3 hours
items.cause: Not enough collagen in the cut, or the oven was too hot.
items.fix: Check the beef every 30 minutes after the 2-hour mark. Chuck and shin can take up to 4 hours. The oven should be at 150C -- no higher. Too-high heat makes the beef tough rather than tender.

content.text: Boeuf bourguignon is the flagship dish of Burgundy, the wine region of central France. The recipe was established as a classic of French cooking in the early 20th century. It became famous internationally through Julia Child's version in 1961. The dish is now made in home kitchens across the world, especially in winter, and is one of the most popular French recipes taught in cooking classes.
